claims.claim: Amphilochius of Iconium was a fourth‑century Christian bishop who governed the see of Iconium (modern Konya, Turkey) from about 374 until his death around 394–403.
He was born around 339/340 in Caesarea in Cappadocia and came from a distinguished Cappadocian family.
One of these surviving sermons is the homily traditionally titled “On Lazarus” (or “On the Four‑day Dead Lazarus”), a sermon on the Gospel account of Jesus raising Lazarus from the dead.

The homily was delivered as a liturgical address to the Christian faithful, celebrating the resurrection of Lazarus as a “firstfruits of the resurrection” and warning against the hostile reaction of the chief priests.
